title: Unbalanced egress surge: asymmetric circuit-breaker trips & coordinated multi-region shed remediation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
On 2026-02-17 22:12 UTC a sudden client egress surge originating from a small APAC customer cohort caused asymmetric queue pressure across two active regions (us-west-2, ap-southeast-1). Local circuit breakers tripped in ap-southeast-1 due to bursty long-sequence requests while us-west-2 remained underutilized. Traffic affinity and sticky routing amplified failover to the congested region, triggering a cascading load-shedding policy that exceeded our 99th-percentile SLO for the Chat API for 27 minutes.

Detection and impact:
- Detection: alerting on 99p latency and circuit-breaker open-rate triggered at 22:14 UTC. Synthetic user probes and customer support reports confirmed degraded client experience by 22:18 UTC.
- Impact: ~6% of production requests experienced latency > 99th percentile and 0.9% experienced 5xx errors due to token-budget exceeded and early-degraded responses. Two paying customers reported increased error rates affecting critical flows.

Root cause analysis (concise):
1) Egress surge source: an external batch job from a single customer sending high-token requests without rate-limits at 22:12 UTC.
2) Affinity routing behavior: request affinity and sticky-region routing directed retries and follow-up requests preferentially to the same region, causing uneven distribution despite global capacity.
3) Circuit breaker configuration: CB threshold logic used per-region absolute concurrency and did not account for request token-cost variance (long sequences tripped CBs faster).
4) Load-shedding policy coupling: the shedding controller prioritized preserving P50 latency metric by shedding long requests first; this unintentionally increased tail latency for short, latency-sensitive requests due to priority inversion inside local priority queues.
5) KV-cache warmup lag: failover to hot region caused many cold KV cache misses increasing per-request runtime and worsening CB trips.

What worked:
- Automated fallback to secondary model variants prevented a full outage for most traffic.
- Circuit-breaker telemetry and sampling allowed us to quickly identify token-cost distribution skew.
- Rollback-safe canary (in place) limited blast radius during mitigation work.

What failed / partial mitigations:
- Global router did not detect and smooth cross-region imbalance quickly enough.
- Shedding heuristics lacked token-awareness and priority fairness; initial mitigation caused a spike in short request latency.

Immediate mitigations applied during the incident (timeline):
- 22:20 UTC: throttled the offending customer IP at the edge (temporary ACL) to stop the source burst.
- 22:24 UTC: relaxed sticky-routing heuristics to prefer capacity-aware routing across regions.
- 22:32 UTC: temporarily lowered long-request priority in local queues to reduce priority inversion.
- 22:39 UTC: warmed KV cache via targeted synthetic prefetch for hot-model prefixes; CB open-rate dropped by 45% in 5 minutes.
- 22:45 UTC: full recovery declared at 22:39–22:45 UTC window once 99p latency returned under SLO and error rate stabilized.

Longer-term root-cause mitigations and design changes proposed:
- Token-aware circuit-breakers: extend CB logic to weight concurrency by estimated token-cost and dynamic sequence-length histograms.
- Cross-region smoothing: implement proactive rebalancing in the global router using sliding-window capacity signals to avoid affinity amplification.
- Priority fairness algorithm: implement a fairness layer that prevents priority inversion when long requests are shed.
- Synthetic warmers and graceful KV migration: pre-warm KV entries on failover and add adaptive warmup budgets.
- Customer rate-limiting: enforce fine-grained per-api-key rate quotas with burst tokens to prevent similar unfettered bursts.

Related artifacts:
- Incident timeline (Chronicle): https://confluence.redwood.ai/chronicles/INC-2026-0217-egress-surge
- Spike analysis doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/spike-egress-surge-analysis-933212
- Production graphs (Datadog): https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors?query=ENG-933212
- GitHub PR for temporary ACL and router change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8124

Recommendation for severity and SLO adjustments:
We recommend a temporary reduction in long-request SLO weight while we roll out token-aware CBs and fairness scheduling. This avoids masking regressions while we build robust admission control.
